Trend chart finite y-axis (200,000 IDR scale). Test data cleanup complete via mongosh.

minor.issue: send_telegram is synchronous (requests.post with timeout=15) called inline inside create_order — blocks the API response by up to 15s if Telegram is slow. Should be moved to BackgroundTasks or asyncio.create_task to avoid blocking the order create response.

Per-artist case-insensitive regex find; for orders with many artists this becomes O(N) sequential round-trips. Acceptable now (artists.length usually <5) but consider bulk find/insert for larger teams.

exchange_rate is a single point-in-time value applied retroactively to ALL historical orders — older IDR orders are converted at TODAY's rate, not the rate at time of order. For accurate historical accounting, store the conversion rate snapshot per order.
fee_freelance is hardcoded as IDR in the conversion (raw_fee/rate) regardless of any future fee currency support. If a USD-paid freelancer ever gets entered, the math will silently divide twice.

action_items: Optional: move Telegram send in create_order/update_order to FastAPI BackgroundTasks so /api/orders POST returns instantly even if Telegram API is slow/unreachable.
Optional: store conversion rate snapshot on each order at create-time (or annotate per-order rate) so historical earnings are stable when settings.exchange_rate changes later.
Optional: tighten fee_freelance currency model — currently assumed always IDR. Add explicit fee_currency field for forward-compat.
Optional: _sync_freelance_artists could use $regex find as bulk operation; not blocking at current scale.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py create_order line 290-305: Telegram send is in-process synchronous requests.post with timeout=15s. Wrap in BackgroundTasks(send_telegram, ...) to avoid blocking POST response on slow networks.

server.py /api/earnings line 456: 'fee_usd = raw_fee / rate' — implicitly assumes fee_freelance is ALWAYS IDR. No assertion or comment in code. Add docstring explaining the convention or introduce fee_currency field.

server.py /api/earnings: exchange_rate read fresh from settings on every call applied to all historical orders → if admin changes rate from 16000 to 17000, ALL past months' USD totals retroactively shift. For accounting this is dangerous; consider per-order rate snapshot.

server.py _sync_freelance_artists line 321: case-insensitive regex without escaping — if an artist name contains regex special chars (e.g. '(', '.', '+') the regex compile will fail or match incorrectly. Use re.escape(name) before interpolation.

Freelance.jsx ProjectModal pickOrder: per-artist split divides fee equally among artists — but if order has mixed Tim+Freelance statuses, the freelancer share might be over-credited (Tim members shouldn't reduce the freelance fee split). Verify business logic with stakeholder.
